Water Research.title: Hydrogel-mediated solar interfacial evaporation for selective lithium and uranium extraction: from coordination mechanisms to engineering scalability.
Water Research.abstract: Lithium (Li+) and uranium (U(VI)) are strategic resources underpinning energy storage, nuclear energy supply and technological security, yet their recovery is governed by fundamentally different chemistries: discrimination arising from Li+ hydration and coordination of uranyl species for U(VI). Against this backdrop, a clear pathway from molecular ion recognition to recoverable Li and U products in complex feeds has yet to emerge. Herein, this review presents a conceptual framework that links hydrogel-mediated solar interfacial evaporation with ion enrichment, selective Li+ and U(VI) recovery, and freshwater production. We first identify the governing functions of these systems, i.e., conversion of solar energy to heat, regulated water supply and control of ion redistribution, and relate them to network architecture and interfacial chemistry. We further distinguish Li+ and U(VI) separation strategies, highlighting hydration-based ion discrimination and uranyl coordination under conditions of low target ion concentrations and strong ionic competition. To address practical deployment, we connect photothermal performance with selective ion mobility and accumulation, as well as the challenges of maintaining stability during larger scale operation. By defining a shared mechanistic framework and reporting criteria, this review highlights the potential of engineered photothermal hydrogels to address pressing demands for the recovery of diverse ions and seeks to inspire broader interest among the green and photothermal research communities.

Water Research.title: Distinct DNA viral ecological responses associated with polystyrene and polyvinyl chloride microplastics in anaerobic digestion of waste activated sludge.
Water Research.abstract: Microplastics are emerging contaminants in waste activated sludge (WAS) that may influence anaerobic digestion (AD), yet their impacts on DNA viral communities remain largely unexplored. Here, we combined metagenomic and metatranscriptomic analysis to investigate DNA viral responses to polystyrene (PS) and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) microplastics in AD of WAS. PS and PVC exerted opposing effects on AD, with PS inhibiting and PVC promoting methane production. PS and PVC triggered distinct viral ecological strategies. PS exposure was linked to increased viral relative abundance, altered community composition, elevated virus-to-host ratios, and upregulated genes encoding structural proteins, indicating enhanced lytic activity. In contrast, PVC exposure was associated with promoted lysogenic maintenance and reduced lytic transcriptional investment, supporting viral-host coexistence. Auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs) related to carbohydrate metabolism displayed divergent relative abundance and expression patterns under PS and PVC exposures. Host prediction revealed extensive virus-host associations among prokaryotes, with microplastic-specific shifts in viral activity. These contrasting viral responses coincided with divergent AD performances, highlighting viruses as previously overlooked components of AD responses to MPs. Our findings suggested that microplastic type was associated with viral infection strategies and regulatory roles in AD, providing novel mechanistic insights into microplastic-induced functional divergence beyond prokaryotic community responses.

Water Research.title: Navigating membrane selection for PFAS removal with permeability-selectivity trade-off and an AI-powered conversational agent.
Water Research.abstract: Nanofiltration (NF) and reverse osmosis (RO) are effective technologies for removing per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) from contaminated water. However, rational membrane design and selection remain constrained by the permeability-selectivity trade-off and complex performance-governing factors. Here, we establish permeability-selectivity relationships for the removal of 17 PFAS species using a curated, literature-derived dataset comprising >1000 data points across 81 polyamide NF and RO membranes. Our analysis reveals that while current membrane innovations advance the performance frontier for a subset of PFAS, commercial membranes still present the leading permeance-selectivity performance for a broad range of PFAS. While these benchmarks define state-of-the-art membrane performance, a gap remains between material-level performance and application-level membrane selection, which requires deriving actionable insights from a large volume of literature data under case-specific constraints. Large language models (LLMs) offer a natural-language interface that allows users to obtain insights within defined constraints, but their reliability in performing such tasks remains unclear. To bridge this gap, we first compare four LLM configurations with progressively structured evidence access and tool use: a Vanilla LLM, LLM with exhaustive context injection (ECI), LLM with single-step retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and LLM with Agentic RAG. LLM with Agentic RAG achieves 96% overall membrane-selection correctness, compared with 73%, 23%, and 1% for single-step RAG, ECI, and the Vanilla LLMs, respectively. With the base model and inference settings held constant, the model performance improves progressively with structured evidence retrieval, adaptive reasoning, and specialized tool use, particularly as the task complexity increases. Building on the LLM with Agentic RAG, we then developed CetaraGPT, an evidence-grounded, user-interactive AI agent that translates quantitative membrane-performance insights into actionable guidance for early-stage membrane screening and evidence-based decision support for PFAS removal.

Water Research.title: Immobilization of nitrogen transforming microorganisms in core-shell gel beads for efficient and simultaneous nitrification-denitrification: Insights into microbial stratification and interaction.
Water Research.abstract: Engineering stable redox stratification within immobilized biomass is crucial for achieving rapid start-up and sustained operation of simultaneous nitrification-denitrification (SND) systems. Here, stratified core-shell gel beads were successfully fabricated using poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)-sodium alginate (SA). Fabrication parameters, including PVA concentration, curing duration, and crosslinking strategy, were optimized to ensure long-term structural stability and appropriate intraparticle mass-transfer characteristics. Sulfate-crosslinked beads incorporating NaHCO3 exhibited favorable oxygen penetration and oxic-anoxic stratification, which were critical for attaining the highest apparent first-order rate constants for NH4+-N and total nitrogen (TN) removal. During long-term operation under varying carbon-to-nitrogen (C/N) ratios (40-10), high removal efficiencies of TN (>92%) and chemical oxygen demand (COD, >93%) were simultaneously achieved at a bulk dissolved oxygen (DO) concentration of 3 mg/L, with minor intermediate accumulation. Oxygen gradients effectively regulated the distribution of oxic and anoxic zones, nitrogen transformation kinetics, and extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) distribution within the beads. Metagenomic analysis suggested spatial partitioning of nitrogen-transforming microorganisms, with ammonia oxidizers (i.e., Nitrosomonas) enriched in oxygen-accessible layers, canonical denitrifying bacteria (DNB, e.g., Rubrivivax and Brevundimonas) preferentially localized in the oxygen-limited regions, and heterotrophic nitrification-aerobic denitrification bacteria (HNADB, e.g., Thauera and Hydrogenophaga) broadly distributed across multiple bead regions. Model simulations indicated greater HNADB- and DNB-associated activities in the exterior and interior, respectively. The developed core-shell system provides a basis for further evaluation under practical wastewater conditions, as it enables rapid system establishment, preserves structural integrity, and maintains stable nitrogen removal performance across a wide range of C/N conditions.

Water Research.title: A micelle-mediated dual coagulation strategy for efficient ciprofloxacin removal: from micelle encapsulation to coagulation mechanism.
Water Research.abstract: Conventional coagulation processes are ineffective for removing soluble antibiotics such as ciprofloxacin (CIP) due to weak coagulant-pollutant interactions and poor settleability of the complexes. Herein, a micelle-mediated dual coagulation strategy is developed that avoids coagulant modification or additional treatment steps. When sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) is added prior to coagulation, spherical micelles are formed and CIP is encapsulated, generating large micelle-CIP aggregates. These aggregates are subsequently removed by dual coagulation with polyaluminum chloride (PAC) and cationic polyacrylamide (CPAM). PAC acts as the primary coagulant, neutralizeing the negatively charged micelle-CIP complexes, while CPAM serves as the secondary flocculant, connecting them into larger and denser aggregates. Under comprehensive optimization of experimental conditions, CIP removal exceeds 91% (up to 93%). Response surface methodology and redundancy analysis identify SDS addition sequence as the most influential factor (79.7% contribution), followed by pH, coexisting ions, and humic acid (HA). Mechanism studies reveal that SDS and CIP associate via hydrophobic interaction and electrostatic attraction. The key contribution lies in establishing a quantitative relationship between micellar morphology and removal efficiency. The critical packing parameter (P) governs micelle morphology, spherical micelles formed under condition P=0.25 (30 mg/L SDS) exhibited the highest encapsulation efficiency for CIP and achieved optimal removal performance. Whereas rod-like micelles at P=0.33-0.42 are less effective. The proposed mechanism expands the previously reported hydrophobic ion-pair mechanism for surfactant-assisted coagulation. This work provides a mechanism-driven approach for antibiotic removal and offers new insights into surfactant-assisted water treatment technologies.

Water Research.title: A novel passive sampler for simultaneous in situ determination of legacy and emerging per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances in wastewaters and urban rivers.
Water Research.abstract: The widespread occurrence of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) in aquatic systems has raised global concern, prompting regulatory actions on several legacy compounds. This study presents a novel diffusive gradients in thin-films (DGT) passive sampler employing a mixed-mode anion exchange (MAX) resin binding layer for simultaneously measuring seven perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids (PFCAs), five perfluoroalkane sulfonic acids (PFSAs), and two emerging replacement PFASs (6:2 FTSA and GenX). Systematic laboratory evaluation demonstrated that the MAX-DGT device performs reliably across wide environmental gradients: pH from 3.0 to 9.0, ionic strength from 0.001 to 0.5 M NaCl, and humic acid as a dissolved organic matter (DOM) surrogate up to 30 mg L-1, with only marginal effects observed at the highest DOM levels. The MAX binding layer exhibits excellent performance under alkaline conditions where earlier weak anion-exchange phases fail. The mass of PFASs accumulated by the sampler increased linearly with deployment time and varied inversely with diffusive layer thickness, consistent with DGT theory. The binding capacity exceeded 550 μg per device, indicating potential applicability in highly contaminated waters. Field deployments at a wastewater treatment plant and in three urban rivers confirmed that the MAX-DGT sampler provided time-weighted average concentrations in close agreement with repeated grab sampling while also responding to episodic contamination events. These results demonstrate the potential of the MAX-DGT as a robust and versatile tool for in situ monitoring of a broad suite of legacy and alternative PFASs in aquatic environments.

Water Research.title: Inactivation of vesicle-cloaked and free murine noroviruses by singlet oxygen and sulfate radicals.
Water Research.abstract: Human norovirus, a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis worldwide, can be shed as vesicle-cloaked virus clusters (viral vesicles) that exhibit enhanced infectivity, virulence, and environmental persistence. Advanced oxidation processes (AOPs), which rely on reactive oxidants, have emerged as promising strategies for virus inactivation. Here, we investigated the inactivation kinetics and mechanisms for vesicle-cloaked and free murine norovirus (MNV-1), a surrogate for human norovirus, under singlet oxygen (1O2) and sulfate radical (SO4•⁻) oxidation. Both reactive oxidants rapidly inactivate vesicle-cloaked and free MNV-1, with second-order disinfection rate constants of ∼108 and ∼108-109 M-1 s-1 for 1O2 and SO4•⁻, respectively. Although MNV-1 vesicles were readily inactivated as infectious units, vesicle membranes protected the cloaked viruses from SO4•⁻-mediated inactivation but provided no protection against 1O2. Oxidation extensively damaged viral and vesicle biomolecules, including genomes, proteins, and lipids, leading to distinct impairments across the viral lifecycle in host cells. Compared with 1O2, SO4•⁻ caused greater reductions in binding to cells and genome replication for both vesicle-cloaked and free MNV-1. In contrast, inhibition of viral/vesicle internalization was more pronounced for vesicle-cloaked MNV-1 regardless of the oxidant. Notably, most vesicle structures remained intact following exposure to either 1O2 or SO4•⁻. Our study establishes a quantitative framework that connects infectivity loss, biomolecular damage, and viral lifecycle impairment in vesicle-cloaked and free viruses under emerging reactive oxidants, providing a mechanistic basis for optimizing AOPs for water disinfection.

Water Research.title: Iron sulfide mineral-mediated autotrophic denitrification: A critical review of electron flow, greenhouse gas dynamics, and environmental performance.
Water Research.abstract: Iron sulfide mineral-mediated autotrophic denitrification (ISAD) uses pyrite, pyrrhotite, and ferrous sulfide as electron donors for nitrate removal with low organic carbon demand, offering potential for sludge reduction and greenhouse gas (GHG) mitigation. However, existing studies have mainly focused on specific systems, particularly constructed wetlands (CWs), with GHG research emphasizing N2O. Nitrogen removal, GHG emissions, resource recovery, and environmental risks have generally been assessed separately. This review establishes a framework linking mineral electron release, interfacial transfer, microbial allocation, and environmental responses. It summarizes the oxidation and electron-transfer properties of major iron sulfide minerals, the resulting Fe-S-N metabolic networks, and their implications for energy use, sludge production, treatment costs, and phosphorus recovery. N2O, CH4, and CO2 are interpreted as interconnected outcomes of Fe-S-NC cycling. The low-carbon performance of ISAD depends on the kinetic coordination of electron release, transfer, and microbial consumption. Insufficient electron supply or terminal reduction may cause N2O accumulation, whereas strongly reducing conditions may favor methanogenesis. Conductive materials, electrochemical enhancement, and composite electron donors can redirect electron flow, although their effectiveness depends on environmental and operational conditions. Sulfate accumulation, iron precipitation, and metal release may further offset environmental benefits. This review provides a framework for jointly optimizing nitrogen removal, GHG mitigation, resource recovery, and environmental safety, and identifies research priorities for sustainable ISAD application.

Water Research.title: Engineering accessible N/O coordination sites in a MOF@COF core-shell adsorbent for rapid and selective copper capture from E-Waste leachates.
Water Research.abstract: Electronic waste represents an important secondary copper resource, yet the rapid and selective recovery of Cu(II) from complex e-waste leachates remains challenging. Herein, NH2-MIL-Fe was employed as a porous scaffold to direct the in situ growth of a TFBE-DHBD-COF shell enriched with imine N and phenolic hydroxyl O sites, thereby regulating the spatial distribution of active sites within the shell and facilitating rapid Cu(II) mass transport and selective binding. The resulting material exhibited rapid adsorption kinetics, reaching equilibrium within 10 min, together with a high maximum Cu(II) adsorption capacity of 776 mg/g. In multicomponent systems, the adsorbent displayed superior affinity toward Cu(II) over competing metal ions. More importantly, it recovered approximately 90% of Cu from a real CPU leachate within 60 min. Experimental characterizations combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that electrostatic enrichment, together with the coordination interactions between Cu(II) and the imine (CN) and hydroxyl groups, dominates the adsorption process. This work provides an effective interfacial engineering strategy for metal recovery from electronic waste.

Water Research.title: Interaction-dependent electron transfer pathways govern the efficiency-stability trade-off of mediators in U(VI) bioelectrochemical remediation.
Water Research.abstract: Practical deployment of bioelectrochemical systems for remediating water contaminated with hexavalent uranium (U(VI)) is constrained by mineral-precipitation-induced electrode passivation during repeated operation. The role of electron mediators in this efficiency-stability trade-off remains unclear. Here, we show that mediator-U(VI) interaction strength is associated with distinct electron-transfer pathways, mineral deposition patterns, and reactor stability. The flavin mononucleotide (FMN)-amended system exhibited impaired interfacial electron transfer and localized mineral accumulation. The anthraquinone-2,6-disulfonate (AQDS)-amended system showed lower charge-transfer resistance, higher electron-transfer capacities, and a more sustained current response. These contrasting observations were interpreted through proposed coordination-dominated and diffusion-facilitated electron-shuttling pathways, respectively. The AQDS-amended system achieved complete aqueous U(VI) removal at C10 and retained 86.03% removal at the end of ten U(VI)-removal cycles (C4-C13). It also showed lower normalized life-cycle impacts across most categories and a calculated direct material-and-energy cost of 71.5 $/kg·U removed. Molecular simulations, electrochemical measurements, microbial-community and biofilm analyses, and uranium-speciation data collectively supported this mediator-dependent mechanism. Under the tested conditions, these findings support considering mediator-U(VI) interactions alongside redox activity when evaluating mediators for repeated U(VI) treatment.

Water Research.title: Polymer-specific eco-coronas redirect microplastic effects in a freshwater macrophyte.
Water Research.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) entering freshwater environments are rapidly transformed by adsorption of environmental biomolecules, creating an eco-corona that redefines their biological identity. Whether this transformation merely alters effect magnitude or redirects biological responses remains unresolved. Here, we compared the effects of pristine and eco-corona-bearing polystyrene (PS) and polylactic acid (PLA) MPs on the freshwater macrophyte Myriophyllum aquaticum by integrating interfacial characterization, plant physiology, metabolomics, and endophytic microbiome profiling. Despite exposure to the same extracellular polymeric substance pool, PS and PLA formed compositionally and structurally distinct eco-coronas. These acquired interfaces altered plant responses in opposing directions relative to their pristine counterparts. The PS eco-corona increased fresh weight by 40.4% relative to pristine PS, moderated oxidative disruption, and supported a recovery-compatible state. In contrast, the PLA eco-corona reduced fresh weight by 18.4% relative to pristine PLA and redirected resource allocation toward an energetically costly defense program. This divergence was linked to contrasting regulation of photosynthetic energy metabolism, redox balance, and secondary metabolism: the PLA eco-corona increased ATPase activity and promoted defense-related metabolite accumulation, whereas the PS eco-corona was associated with photosynthetic recovery and repair-related metabolic pathways. Host metabolic reprogramming further coincided with distinct patterns of endophytic microbiome assembly, consistent with a metabolic-filtering framework. These findings show that MP effects emerge from interactions between polymer chemistry and environmentally acquired interfaces, and that assessments based solely on pristine particles may misrepresent the direction and magnitude of changes in plant physiology, metabolism, and the associated microbiome.

Water Research.title: Advancing structural interpretability in multispecies aquatic toxicity prediction through feature-wise conditioning in multimodal graph neural networks.
Water Research.abstract: Ecological risk assessment requires aquatic toxicity estimates for untested chemical-species combinations. Predictive models can combine molecular structure with physicochemical, species, and exposure information to estimate these toxicities. We examined how this integration affects prediction and structural interpretation. Conventional concatenation joins encoded molecular features with other inputs. We compared this with feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM), which adjusts molecular features using those inputs. FiLM-Concat additionally concatenates these inputs with adjusted features. Using 2,943 LC50 records for 226 chemicals and 18 species, we compared four encoders and three fusion strategies across ten repeated CAS-grouped splits. Within 3D GINE, FiLM-Concat yielded the highest mean test R2 (0.555 ± 0.091), but predictive superiority over concatenation was not established (corrected resampled p = 0.236). GNNExplainer assessed atom importance. At 25% retained atoms with other inputs unchanged, Fidelity- was lower for FiLM-Concat than concatenation (0.725 vs. 0.900; corrected resampled p = 0.0447), a nominal result specific to this retention fraction. Lower Fidelity- reflects prediction preservation by the retained subgraph together with the unchanged inputs and does not isolate the contribution of the retained atoms. Selected local maps illustrated chemical-specific similarities and differences rather than validated toxicophores. Species-dependent attribution occurred across fusion strategies in 46 held-out chemicals. Frozen external evaluation of 80 LC50 records from 27 development-excluded chemicals yielded mean R2 of 0.549-0.584 within represented species. FiLM-Concat combines competitive prediction with exploratory structural attribution, supporting model inspection and chemical hypothesis generation rather than established mechanistic or predictive superiority.

Water Research.title: Post-disturbance aggregate morphology and rapid flotation of filamentous cyanobacteria.
Water Research.abstract: Surface accumulation of filamentous cyanobacteria threatens water quality in managed waterways. We examined the morphology and vertical motion of aggregates formed by a heterocystous filamentous cyanobacterial isolate after a standardized three-cycle manual shaking protocol at two working volumes (250 and 500 mL). Aggregate imaging, RGB-based surface biomass estimation, planar particle image velocimetry (PIV), and dissolved oxygen measurements were used to characterize post-disturbance dynamics. Among 402 trackable aggregates (maximum Feret diameter > 0.5 mm), most were 1-3 mm in the 250-mL configuration (81.8%) and 1-4 mm in the 500-mL configuration (83.3%), a pattern consistent across three sampling phases; aggregates exceeding 4 mm accounted for 15.4% of observations at 500 mL versus 3.3% at 250 mL. The pooled size-binned mean ascent velocity was highest in the 1-2 mm bin (4.6 mm/s), individual velocities exceeded 11 mm/s, and larger bins generally had lower means. In the 500-mL configuration, surface accumulation accelerated from approximately 73 s after shaking ceased, while flow fluctuations measured in separate PIV runs declined. In a separate static observation, oxygen supersaturation developed while aggregates remained at the bottom. These observations are consistent with a turbulence-decay hypothesis linking post-disturbance flow relaxation, aggregate size structure, and flotation. Because a single forcing protocol was used and working volume also changed biomass and depth, the causal aggregation sequence, any critical forcing threshold, and the role of bubble retention require targeted tests across forcing intensities and spatial scales.

Water Research.title: Ecosystem modeling links water quality, carrying capacity, nutrient removal, and economic returns in integrated shrimp pond aquaculture.
Water Research.abstract: Integrated aquaculture can reduce nutrients while sustaining production, yet quantitative methods for selecting species combinations and stocking ratios remain limited. We developed a pond ecosystem model for an intensive Litopenaeus vannamei system integrated with the filter-feeding clam mercenaria and the floating bed plant Sesuvium portulacastrum. Calibration and performance evaluation used the same 105-day pond dataset; organism growth and major nutrient dynamics were reproduced with R2 of 0.80 to 0.98 and relative root mean square error of 5.42% to 18.77%. Carrying capacities were assessed against tailwater total nitrogen, total phosphorus, and clam marketable-size requirements. At 1.5% floating-bed coverage, estimated carrying capacities of L. vannamei and M. mercenaria were 26.86 and 34.30 ind m-2, respectively. Relative to current stocking densities at the same coverage, profit increased from 9008.45 to 17,376.90 $ ha-1 per cycle (+92.9%), and the combined monetary value of nitrogen and phosphorus removal increased from 39.95 to 107.17 $ ha-1 per cycle (+168.2%). Exploratory simulations at 9.0% and 18.0% coverage predicted further profit increases of 5.9% and 13.0%, and nutrient removal value increases of 56.1% and 118.0%, respectively, relative to the carrying capacity at 1.5% coverage. This study provides a quantitative framework for assessing carrying capacity under specified nutrient and marketable-size constraints, designing multispecies stocking strategies, and balancing economic returns with nutrient removal in intensive aquaculture ponds.

Water Research.title: DOM-birnessite association modes regulate electron-accepting capacity and hydroxyl radical production during redox cycling.
Water Research.abstract: Redox fluctuations at sediment-water interfaces can drive element cycling and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, with implications for contaminant fate and water quality. Yet how the association modes between dissolved organic matter (DOM) and manganese oxides regulate these ROS pulses remains poorly understood. Here, we compared birnessite (Bir) associated with DOM via adsorption (Bir@DOMads) and coprecipitation (Bir@DOMcop) over a reduction-oxidation cycle. Relative to Bir and DOM alone, Bir@DOMcop increased hydroxyl radical (•OH) production by up to 2.32- and 3.65-fold, while Bir@DOMads enhanced it by 1.65- and 2.62-fold, respectively. The association modes critically affected the ROS responses. Coprecipitation yielded a higher average Mn oxidation state and stronger Mn-O/Mn-Mn coordination, suggesting differences in the local Mn environment. Accordingly, Bir@DOMcop had a threefold higher electron-accepting capacity and a greater contact potential difference (157 ± 14 mV), as determined by atomic force microscopy-based Kelvin probe force microscopy, indicating enhanced electron uptake during reduction. The resulting pool of more reduced Mn species then donated electrons to O2 upon reoxidation, boosting •OH production. In contrast, adsorbed DOM enhanced •OH generation despite weaker direct electron transfer. Rotating ring-disk electrode (RRDE) measurements revealed substantially higher H2O2 selectivity for Bir@DOMads10:1 (45.35%) than for Bir and Bir@DOMcop10:1, supporting an enhanced contribution of the two-electron O2 reduction pathway. Collectively, these findings identify mineral@DOM-water interfaces as potential hotspots of ROS pulses in dynamic redox settings of sediments and soils.

Science Bulletin.title: Targeting mitochondrial dysfunction and ferroptosis in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by a self-assembled nanomedicine with dual functions: GPX4 mimicry and energy metabolism restoration.
Science Bulletin.abstract: Neuronal apoptosis induced by mitochondrial dysfunction and neuronal ferroptosis induced by glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) inactivation are the root causes of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI). Inspired by the "catalytic tetrad" of the GPX4 catalytic center, this study ingeniously developed a self-driving neural guardian nanomedicine (SNG). SNG successfully retains the most critical selenol group for GPX4's catalytic function and a strategically positioned carboxyl group in close proximity, allowing SNG to exhibit excellent GPX-mimicking activity. Due to the genipin-like group, SNG can autonomously navigate to target ischemic brain areas, and further precisely anchor to neuronal mitochondria. Based on its potent GPX4 mimetic activity and released active Se, SNG can fundamentally reverse neuronal ferroptosis. Furthermore, SNG itself possesses antioxidant properties and can spontaneously degrade to release genipin. Therefore, it ameliorates neuronal mitochondrial dysfunction during CIRI through the dual effects of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) scavenging and inhibition of excessive activation of mitochondrial uncoupling protein 2 (UCP2). SNG suppresses the release of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), which subsequently inhibits inflammation. This work provides a breakthrough approach for the treatment of CIRI by synergistically inhibiting neuronal ferroptosis, neuronal apoptosis, and neuroinflammation, while also offering new directions for the treatment of other ischemia-reperfusion diseases.

Science Bulletin.title: Quantifying global cryosphere-linked sustainable development progress.
Science Bulletin.abstract: Progress toward the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development remains uneven, with many of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) global targets out of reach. Climate warming is accelerating unprecedented cryosphere retreat, compounding pressures on SDG achievement across high-mountain and polar regions. Despite this escalating crisis, systematic quantitative assessments that explicitly resolve the spatiotemporal linkages between cryosphere dynamics and SDG trajectories remain critically scarce. To address this gap, we introduce an integrated analytical framework termed 'the cryo-SDGs', designed to evaluate progress on SDG indicators across global cryospheric regions. From 2000 to 2023, the study-specific cryo-SDGs composite index increased by 25.3%, revealing a positive trend across seven major domains. Pathway analyses identify cryo-SDG 2 (Zero Hunger) and cryo-SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation) as the most prominent associators. Our findings highlight the critical need to align SDG prioritization with the cascading effects of cryosphere degradation, a precondition for fulfilling post‑2030 sustainability commitments in cryospheric regions. Without embedding cryosphere science into sustainability planning, efforts to build an equitable and resilient future of regions depending on cryosphere services will remain incomplete.

Science Bulletin.title: Recursive synthetic data training degrades medical foundation models.
The ZmGPAT6-ZmMPK2/7-ZmPIP2;1 fine-regulated module confers salt-alkali tolerance via controlling H(2)O(2) transport in maize.
Science Bulletin.abstract: Soil salinization and alkalization represent major abiotic stresses that severely constrain global agricultural sustainability, crop productivity, and food security. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying plant adaptation to both stresses are far from being fully resolved. Here, we identify a salt-alkali stress-responsive gene, ZmGPAT6, encoding a glycerol-3-phosphate acyltransferase (GPAT) with dual enzymatic activities of acyltransferase and phosphatase. ZmGPAT6 catalyzes the production of lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) and monoacylglycerol (MAG), resulting in the decline of phosphatidic acid (PA). PA binds to and activates ZmMPK2 and ZmMPK7 kinases, which interact with and phosphorylate the aquaporin ZmPIP2;1, thereby facilitating H2O2 transport in maize leaves and roots. However, ZmGPAT6 interacts with and directly dephosphorylates ZmMPK2/7 and ZmPIP2;1, consequently inhibiting ZmPIP2;1-driven H2O2 transport. Both salt and alkali stresses induce ZmGPAT6 expression in maize leaves and roots, leading to reduced PA accumulation and thus decreasing the phosphorylation level of ZmPIP2;1 by ZmMPK2/7. Simultaneously, the stress-induced accumulation of ZmGPAT6 enhances the dephosphorylation levels of ZmMPK2/7 and ZmPIP2;1. Under both stress conditions, the ZmGPAT6-ZmMPK2/7-ZmPIP2;1 module dually restricts H2O2 transport, leading to H2O2 over-accumulation in leaves and roots and impairing maize growth. Our findings reveal a direct linkage between ZmGPAT6-mediated lipid metabolism and ZmMPK2/7-driven phosphorylation of ZmPIP2;1 required for H2O2 transport, thus offering novel insights and potential genetic targets for improving salt-alkali tolerance in maize.

Here, the authors report the realization of multifunctional strained 2D MoS2 devices on patterned HfO2 substrates, showing synaptic memory or high-mobility transistors functionalities depending on the carrier transport direction.

Nature Communications.title: G3BP1-induced retrograde transport blockade triggers HSC activation and liver fibrosis via COPI alternative splicing
Nature Communications.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79478-6Liver fibrosis is driven by hepatic stellate cell activation, but its molecular drivers remain unclear. Here, the authors show that G3BP1 promotes COPI alternative splicing via SRPK1–hnRNPM, impairing Golgi-to-ER transport and causing ER stress that activates these cells and drives fibrosis.

Nature Communications.title: Structural basis for constitutive activation of oncogenic gp130 mutants found in human inflammatory hepatocellular adenomas
Nature Communications.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79742-9Inflammatory hepatocellular adenomas are benign liver tumors primarily driven by constitutively active gp130 mutants. The authors employ cryo-EM and mutagenesis to reveal the structural mechanism of ligand-independent activation of these mutants.

Nature Communications.title: Biosynthesis of iboga alkaloids
Nature Communications.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79750-9Tabernanthe iboga produces the medically important alkaloids voacangine and ibogaine, but key steps in their biosynthesis, as well as the biosynthetic route to the structurally distinct alkaloid ibophyllidine, have remained unresolved. Using genome sequencing, bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, and biochemical reconstitution, the authors identify the missing enzymes required for coronaridine and voacangine biosynthesis, elucidate the complete pathway to ibophyllidine, and achieve heterologous production of voacangine in Nicotiana benthamiana.

Nature Communications.title: Visible light drives bright extreme-ultraviolet high harmonics
Nature Communications.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79615-1High-harmonic generation (HHG) brings bright extreme ultraviolet (XUV) light to the laboratory, but achieving high photon flux at short wavelengths remains a challenge. Here, the authors demonstrate visible-light-driven HHG with exceptionally high flux at 13.5 nm, enabled by plasma-core-induced self-guiding and efficient phase-matching conditions.

Nature Communications.title: Accelerating high-throughput catalyst screening by direct generation of equilibrium adsorption structures
Nature Communications.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79243-9The authors develop DBCata, a generative model trained without energy or force labels to produce near-equilibrium adsorption structures, enabling faster screening of candidate catalysts.

Nature Communications.title: Mapping temperature using transmission Kikuchi diffraction
Nature Communications.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77502-3Measuring nanoscale temperatures is hard: contact probes perturb samples and optical methods lack resolution. Here, authors develop Kikuchi diffraction thermometry, a non-contact electron microscopy method that maps nanoscale temperatures via tiny heat-induced lattice changes.

Nature Communications.title: Entropy-engineered polar heterogeneity enables near-decoupled polarization–strain behavior for high-density energy storage
Nature Communications.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79625-zStrong polarization–strain coupling limits the energy density and reliability of lead-free dielectric capacitors. Here, the authors show that entropy-engineered polar heterogeneity weakens this coupling, enabling ultrahigh energy storage with minimal electrostrain.

Nature Communications.title: Shape conforming Janus hydrogel for preventing anastomotic leaks
Nature Communications.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79644-wAnastomotic leaks remain a major complication of gastrointestinal surgery, yet existing sealants often fail to provide durable coverage of irregular tissue surfaces. Here, the authors develop a Janus powder-derived dressing composed of an adhesive porous layer mechanically interlocked with a non-adhesive backing. The material conforms to anastomotic tissues, resists unwanted post-surgical adhesions, and provides sustained sealing, offering a promising strategy for leak prevention and repair.

Nature Communications.title: A global atlas of digital dermatology to map innovation and disparities
Nature Communications.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78602-wThe authors map 1.1 million dermatology images to assess the diversity of data used to train AI and find major gaps in darker skin tones and children, highlighting the importance of representation for future data collection.

Nature Communications.title: Deep ultraviolet gallium-oxide avalanche photodiodes reaching an impulse-response-derived gain-bandwidth record of 152 GHz
Nature Communications.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79355-2Solar-blind gallium oxide photodetectors enable secure deep-ultraviolet communication but face a trade-off between speed and gain. Dong et al. engineered a multilayer avalanche device achieving nanosecond response, high gain, and a record gain-bandwidth product.

Molecular Biology and Evolution.title: Early histological remission and prognosis in inflammatory bowel disease: a nationwide cohort study
Molecular Biology and Evolution.abstract: AbstractBackground & AimsEarly remission in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is increasingly recognized for providing long-term prognostic benefits, despite limited supporting data. We examined the prognostic value of histological remission within 12 months of diagnosis.MethodsA nationwide cohort study of 14 019 Swedish IBD patients diagnosed in 1990-2022. These patients underwent ileo-colorectal biopsies showing histological remission or inflammation within 1-ResultsEarly histological remission was more prevalent in patients with higher educational attainment or those diagnosed since 2000, but less common in childhood-onset (ConclusionsSustained histological inflammation (vs remission) 12 months after IBD diagnosis predicted a higher risk of treatment failure and CRC, indicating that early histological remission may improve long-term disease prognosis.
